script.speaker: W
script.text: Haven't the revised budget figures been circulated to the regional managers yet?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Only the ones in Asia-Pacific have them so far.
No, the figures were revised by Finance.
I prefer the circulation of the news magazine.
questions.explanation: A is a partial but direct answer: some regions have the figures, others do not. B repeats 'revised' without answering whether they were sent. C is a sound-alike distractor ('circulated' / 'circulation').

script.speaker: M
script.text: Who's in charge of renewing the maintenance contract this year?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Yes, it was renewed last March.
Didn't Ms. Okafor's team take that over?
The contract is about twelve pages long.
questions.explanation: B answers a 'who' question indirectly by naming a team, in the form of a confirming question. A is a Yes/No answer to a Wh- question. C reuses 'contract' but says nothing about who is responsible.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Would you rather present the quarterly results yourself, or have Daniel do it?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Quarterly results are due on Friday.
I'm leaving for the airport right after lunch, so you'd better ask Daniel.
questions.explanation: B gives a reason the speaker cannot present and so implies the answer: Daniel. A repeats 'quarterly results'. C answers an either/or question with 'Yes'.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Why was the shipment of display cases held up at customs?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Yes, the cases are in the showroom.
It's customary to hold them there.
A few of the forms were missing signatures.
questions.explanation: C gives a plausible reason. A starts with 'Yes' to a Wh- question. B is a sound-alike distractor ('customs' / 'customary') and misuses 'held'.

script.speaker: W
script.text: I thought the training session was supposed to be mandatory.

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Yes, the supposed deadline is Monday.
It was, until the executive team revised the policy.
questions.explanation: A statement with 'I thought...' invites a correction. C ('It was, until...') corrects the assumption. A and B recycle sounds or words ('training' / 'train', 'supposed') without responding.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Gregor, did you see the email from Halvorsen Packaging? They're pushing back the delivery of our new cartons to the twentieth.

script.speaker: M
script.text: That's a week after the product launch. We can't ship pre-orders without packaging.

script.speaker: W
script.text: I know. Our other supplier, Brightline, could fill the order, but their minimum quantity is double what we normally buy.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Double is too much storage for our warehouse. How about asking Brightline to split the order into two deliveries, one now and one after the launch?

script.speaker: W
script.text: Good idea. I'll call them this afternoon. And could you let the marketing team know the launch date might need to be adjusted if that falls through?

script.speaker: M
script.text: Will do. I'll send them a note after lunch.

questions.prompt: What problem are the speakers discussing?
options: A product launch has been cancelled.
questions.explanation: Halvorsen Packaging is 'pushing back' the delivery of cartons, which means the delivery will be late. The launch is not cancelled; its date might be adjusted only if the backup plan fails.

questions.prompt: What does the man propose?
options: Having the second supplier deliver in two shipments
Moving the launch to the twentieth
questions.explanation: He suggests asking Brightline to 'split the order into two deliveries'. Doubling is the supplier's minimum, which he rejects because of storage space.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Priya, I looked over the vendor comparison. The Lisbon hotel is cheaper, but I noticed the quote doesn't include the conference room rental.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Right, that's charged per half day. Once you add it, the two venues come within about two hundred euros of each other.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Then it comes down to location. Most of our attendees will be flying into Madrid, and Lisbon adds a connecting flight for many of them.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Good point. Let's go with Madrid. I'll tell the hotel we want to hold the block of rooms until Friday, so please send me the final headcount by Thursday.

script.speaker: M
script.text: I'll have it to you by Wednesday.

questions.prompt: Why does the man say, "it comes down to location"?
options: The price difference is too large to ignore.
Cost no longer separates the two options.
questions.explanation: Once the room rental is added, the venues are within about 200 euros, so price is no longer the deciding factor and location is.

questions.prompt: When will the man provide the headcount?
questions.explanation: The woman asks for it 'by Thursday', but the man promises it 'by Wednesday'. Friday is the hotel's room-hold deadline.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Mr. Delgado, the auditors will be on site Monday, and the finance system has been sluggish since the update.

script.speaker: M
script.text: IT told me the patch should be fixed by tonight, but I wouldn't count on it. Can your team export the quarter's transactions to a spreadsheet as a backup?

script.speaker: W
script.text: We can, though reconciling them manually would take two people the entire weekend.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Then let's do it only if the system is still slow at six. Check with IT at that point and call me either way.

questions.prompt: What is the woman concerned about?
questions.explanation: She mentions the upcoming audit on Monday and that the finance system has been sluggish.

questions.prompt: What will the woman most likely do at six o'clock?
options: Contact IT and call the man
questions.explanation: The man says to check with IT at six and call him either way. Exporting happens only if the system is still slow, and reconciling is a later, manual step.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we start the shift, a quick update on the new safety procedures. Starting Monday, all visitors to the assembly floor must wear a badge in addition to protective eyewear. The badges will be issued at the front desk, not by individual supervisors as before. Also, because of the construction on Dock Road, delivery trucks will use the north gate between seven and nine a.m. If you normally park near the north gate, please use Lot C instead. Finally, the quarterly safety drill, originally planned for Tuesday, has been moved to Thursday afternoon so that it doesn't conflict with the inventory count. Questions can go to Ms. Tanaka in Facilities.

questions.prompt: What is changing about the visitor badges?
questions.explanation: Badges will be issued at the front desk 'not by individual supervisors as before', so the issuer changes.

questions.prompt: Why are some employees asked to use Lot C?
options: Delivery trucks will be using the north gate.
It is closer to the assembly floor.
A safety drill will be held nearby.
Visitors will park near the north gate.
questions.explanation: Trucks will use the north gate between seven and nine a.m. because of construction, so people who normally park there should use Lot C.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the safety drill?
options: It will still take place on Tuesday.
It was rescheduled to avoid a conflict.
It will be longer than last time.
questions.explanation: It moved from Tuesday to Thursday afternoon so it would not conflict with the inventory count.

questions.prompt: The warranty covers repairs ------ the product is used in accordance with the instruction manual.
questions.explanation: A conjunction expressing a condition is needed before a full clause. 'As long as' = on the condition that. 'In case of' needs a noun phrase; 'even though' is concessive; 'so that' expresses purpose.

questions.prompt: Ms. Reyes, ------ proposal was approved last week, will lead the pilot program.
questions.explanation: A possessive relative pronoun is needed to link 'Ms. Reyes' and 'proposal': 'whose proposal'.

questions.prompt: The auditor's report highlighted several ------ in the company's inventory tracking procedures.
questions.explanation: 'Discrepancies' = inconsistencies between records and reality, the usual collocation with auditing and inventory.

questions.prompt: Neither the project manager nor the engineers ------ been informed of the revised deadline.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'engineers' (plural). 'Have been informed' also needs the perfect auxiliary, not 'were' or 'is'.

questions.prompt: Sales of the new product line were ------ higher than projected, prompting the company to double its production.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the comparative adjective 'higher'.

questions.prompt: The two departments will ------ their budgets to avoid duplicate software purchases.
questions.explanation: 'Consolidate' = combine into one, which is how duplicate purchases are avoided. The other verbs do not fit the object 'budgets'.

From: Helena Brandt, Procurement Manager
To: All Department Heads
Subject: Revised approval limits for purchase requests
Date: March 3

Dear colleagues,

Effective April 1, purchase requests exceeding $2,500 will require the signature of a second approver in addition to the department head. This change follows an internal review that found several orders had been placed without comparing at least two quotes. Requests under the threshold will continue to follow the current one-step process, and recurring subscriptions are exempt provided they were approved before April 1.

To avoid delays, please submit larger requests at least five business days before the needed delivery date. A summary table and the new form are attached. If your team has pending orders that will cross the threshold, contact me before March 20 so that we can arrange an exception where appropriate.

Regards,
Helena Brandt

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the email?
options: To announce a change to an approval process
To request price quotes from vendors
To introduce a new procurement manager
questions.explanation: The email announces that, from April 1, larger purchase requests need a second approver.

questions.prompt: Who is asked to contact Ms. Brandt before March 20?
options: Vendors who want approval to supply goods
Department heads with pending orders that will exceed the threshold
questions.explanation: Teams with pending orders that will cross the $2,500 threshold are asked to contact her so an exception can be arranged.

docs.label: Services Agreement (excerpt)
docs.text:
7. Termination

7.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to the other party.

7.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches any provision and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice specifying the breach.

7.3 Upon termination, Supplier shall refund any prepaid fees attributable to services not yet performed, and Client shall pay for all services performed through the effective date of termination.

7.4 Sections 5 (Confidentiality) and 9 (Limitation of Liability) shall survive termination.

questions.prompt: According to the clause, what must happen before a party can end the agreement because of a breach?
options: The other party must be given written notice and thirty days to fix the problem.
The terminating party must give sixty days' written notice.
The Supplier must refund all prepaid fees.
Both parties must agree in writing to the termination.
questions.explanation: Under 7.2, termination for breach is available only if the breaching party fails to cure within 30 days after written notice. The 60-day notice in 7.1 applies to termination for convenience.

questions.prompt: What is indicated about confidentiality obligations?
options: They end when the agreement is terminated.
They apply only to the Supplier.
They are replaced by the Limitation of Liability.
questions.explanation: Section 7.4 says Sections 5 and 9 'survive termination', so confidentiality continues after the agreement ends.

docs.label: Text-message chain
docs.text:
Marcus Lee [2:14 P.M.]
Did the Osaka client confirm the Thursday call?

Dana Whitfield [2:16 P.M.]
Not yet. Their assistant said Mr. Ito is traveling and may only be reachable after his flight lands.

Marcus Lee [2:17 P.M.]
Then we may be presenting without the final pricing sheet. Legal still hasn't signed off on the discount tiers.

Dana Whitfield [2:19 P.M.]
I wouldn't hold off. Legal usually clears things the same day they see them.

Marcus Lee [2:20 P.M.]
Fair enough. I'll send them the draft now and flag it as urgent.

Dana Whitfield [2:21 P.M.]
Do that. And I'll ask the assistant to propose a backup slot Friday morning.

questions.prompt: At 2:19 P.M., what does Ms. Whitfield most likely mean when she writes, "I wouldn't hold off"?
options: She does not want to host the call on Thursday.
She thinks the discount tiers should be changed.
She believes preparation should continue without waiting.
She plans to wait for the client's flight to land.
questions.explanation: Mr. Lee worries about presenting without the pricing sheet. She replies that Legal usually clears items quickly, so there is no need to delay (hold off) preparing.

questions.prompt: What will Mr. Lee most likely do next?
questions.explanation: He says, 'I'll send them the draft now and flag it as urgent.' 'Them' refers to Legal. Ms. Whitfield, not Mr. Lee, will ask about a Friday slot.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Should we reserve the larger room, even though only twelve people have confirmed?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Let’s wait until the registration deadline tomorrow.
It is on the larger shelf.
questions.explanation: The reply proposes delaying the room decision until attendance is clearer. The other choices do not address which room to book.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Hasn’t the replacement scanner arrived yet?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: It was delivered, but it is still being configured.
questions.explanation: The equipment has arrived but is not ready for use. A repeats the action of scanning rather than answering the delivery question.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Who can approve this expense while Elena is away?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: She approved the itinerary last month.
questions.explanation: The deputy is authorized to approve expenses. The past approval of an itinerary does not identify the substitute approver.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Would you mind checking the figures before I send the proposal?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Of course not; give me ten minutes.
questions.explanation: Of course not accepts a request phrased with Would you mind. The speaker asks for time to check the figures.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Why don’t we use last year’s photographs in the brochure?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: I used to read that brochure.
questions.explanation: The reply explains why reusing the photographs would be unsuitable: the product packaging has changed.

script.speaker: M
script.text: The maintenance team can come either this afternoon or Friday morning.

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Friday works, provided they finish before our noon inspection.
The inspection report is in the folder.
questions.explanation: The response selects Friday and adds a condition. The other statements do not choose an appointment.

script.speaker: W
script.text: The new display panels won’t reach the shop until Wednesday. The preview is Tuesday evening.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Could we move the preview?

script.speaker: W
script.text: Invitations have already gone out. But the supplier has two demonstration panels we could borrow. They would need collecting by four on Tuesday.

script.speaker: M
script.text: I’m meeting a client until three thirty. I’ll ask Noor to collect them and I’ll handle the setup when I get back.

questions.prompt: What has caused a problem?
options: Some display panels will arrive too late.
questions.explanation: The panels arrive Wednesday, after the Tuesday preview. Invitations have already been sent, which makes rescheduling difficult.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman mention the invitations?
options: To explain why changing the event is inconvenient
questions.explanation: Her response rejects the proposed date change by pointing out that guests have already been notified.

questions.prompt: What will the man do next?
options: Contact Noor about collecting the panels
questions.explanation: He says he will ask Noor to collect the demonstration panels. He will set them up later, after his client meeting.

script.speaker: M
script.text: I thought the quote for the office move included packing.

script.speaker: W
script.text: It covers crates and transport. Packing by the movers costs an extra six hundred dollars.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Our team could pack the files, but not the monitors. Could they quote for the monitors only?

script.speaker: W
script.text: I’ll ask. We need a revised written estimate before Finance meets on Thursday.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Please request it for Wednesday noon so I have time to check it.

questions.prompt: What is included in the current quote?
questions.explanation: The woman explicitly states that crates and transport are included. Packing is an additional service.

questions.prompt: What does the man want the movers to pack?
questions.explanation: The staff can pack files, but not monitors. He requests a separate quote for packing only the monitors.

questions.prompt: When does the man want the revised estimate?
questions.explanation: Finance meets Thursday, but the requested deadline is Wednesday noon to allow a review beforehand.

script.speaker: N
script.text: This message is for members of Harbor Museum. From June first, the west entrance will close for repairs. Please use the garden entrance, which is accessible from Pine Street. Members may still enter thirty minutes before public opening, except on Mondays, when staff training takes place. If you booked a June workshop before May twentieth, your confirmation may show the old entrance. Your booking remains valid; no new ticket is required.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the message?
options: To explain a temporary entrance change
questions.explanation: The announcement explains where visitors should enter during repairs. Existing workshop bookings remain valid.

questions.prompt: When is early admission unavailable?
questions.explanation: The early-entry benefit continues except on Mondays because staff training takes place then.

questions.prompt: What should someone with an older workshop confirmation do?
options: Use the garden entrance with the existing booking
Wait until the repairs are finished
questions.explanation: The entrance information may be outdated, but the booking remains valid and no replacement ticket is needed.

questions.prompt: Not until the final inspection is complete _____ the equipment be put into service.
questions.explanation: An initial negative expression such as Not until requires auxiliary–subject inversion: will the equipment be put into service.

questions.prompt: The hotel agreed to _____ the cancellation fee because the flight had been grounded.
questions.explanation: To waive a fee means to decide not to charge it. A canceled flight provides the reason for this exception.

questions.prompt: Applications received after Friday will be considered only if positions remain _____.
questions.explanation: Remain is a linking verb here and takes the adjective available, describing the positions.

questions.prompt: The two departments must _____ their schedules before announcing a launch date.
questions.explanation: Coordinate schedules means to organize them so that the activities work together. Comply requires with and does not take schedules directly.

questions.prompt: The supplier, _____ proposal included on-site training, was selected unanimously.
questions.explanation: Whose expresses possession: the supplier’s proposal included training. The other relative pronouns cannot directly modify proposal here.

questions.prompt: _____ the initial cost is higher, the new system should reduce maintenance expenses.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a full concessive clause. Despite and Because of require a noun phrase; Unless would change the intended contrast.

questions.prompt: The consultant’s report offers a _____ assessment of both the benefits and the risks.
questions.explanation: A balanced assessment gives fair consideration to competing factors, here both benefits and risks.

questions.prompt: The director requested that each invoice _____ checked against the purchase order.
questions.explanation: A request clause can use the mandative subjunctive: requested that each invoice be checked. Be remains in the base form regardless of the singular subject.

docs.text:
To: Branch managers
Subject: Equipment collection

Starting July 8, used laptops must be sent to our central office rather than directly to the recycler. This change will allow our technicians to [1] that all business data has been removed.

Please attach a completed inventory form to each shipment. Packages [2] a form will be held until the sender supplies one. [3]

The new procedure applies to laptops only. Other equipment should [4] be sent directly to the approved recycler. Thank you for helping us keep accurate disposal records.

questions.prompt: Select the best word for [1].
questions.explanation: Verify means confirm through checking. The technicians need to confirm data removal rather than assume or predict it.

questions.prompt: Select the best word for [2].
questions.explanation: Without a form describes a package lacking the required document. Unless would need a clause.

questions.prompt: Select the best sentence for [3].
options: The recycler now offers lower prices.
New computers will arrive next month.
Employees may work remotely on Fridays.
A blank copy of the form is attached for your convenience.
questions.explanation: The paragraph explains the mandatory inventory form. A sentence pointing to an attached blank form directly supports that instruction.

questions.prompt: Select the best word for [4].
questions.explanation: Still signals continuation: only the laptop procedure changes, while the existing route for other equipment remains in effect.

The copier is beside the door.

script.speaker: M

options: Not before the architect returns tomorrow.

script.speaker: W

options: I can borrow a few from the room next door.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Would the morning delivery slot suit you?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: Only if the driver can arrive after ten.
questions.explanation: The response conditionally accepts the suggested slot. Suit here means be convenient, not an item of clothing.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Who should receive the signed agreement?

questions.prompt: Mark your answer.
options: The legal team asked for the original.
The signature is at the bottom.
We reached an agreement last week.
questions.explanation: The legal team is identified as the intended recipient. Neither the location of a signature nor the agreement date answers Who.

script.speaker: W
script.text: The client demonstration needs a wired connection. Room B is free at two, but it only has wireless internet.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Room D has a cable connection. It is reserved until two thirty, though.

script.speaker: W
script.text: The client can start at three. Could you change our reservation and ask Facilities to test the cable first?

script.speaker: M
script.text: Yes. I’ll book Room D for three and contact Facilities now.

questions.prompt: Why is Room B unsuitable?
options: It lacks the required wired connection.
questions.explanation: The demonstration specifically requires a wired connection. Room B has wireless internet only; no problem with size or projection is stated.

questions.prompt: When will the demonstration begin?
questions.explanation: Two is the original room availability and two thirty is when Room D becomes free. The agreed demonstration time is three.

questions.prompt: What will the man ask Facilities to do?
questions.explanation: The woman asks for the cable to be tested before the demonstration, and the man agrees to contact Facilities.

script.speaker: M
script.text: We found a price error on page twelve of the catalog. Only the printed version is affected; the website is correct.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Has the shipment to dealers left?

script.speaker: M
script.text: Not yet, but the printer says a full reprint would take a week.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Then let’s insert a correction sheet into each copy. I’ll send you the wording this morning.

script.speaker: M
script.text: Good. I’ll ask the warehouse to hold the cartons until the inserts arrive.

questions.prompt: Where does the error appear?
questions.explanation: The man says only the printed version is affected. The website already has the correct information.

questions.prompt: Why do the speakers choose correction sheets?
options: Dealers asked for a larger catalog.
A full reprint would delay the work.
The printer has run out of paper.
questions.explanation: A reprint would take a week. The correction inserts provide an alternative without waiting for all catalogs to be reprinted.

questions.prompt: What will the man arrange?
options: A temporary hold on the cartons
questions.explanation: He will ask the warehouse to hold the cartons until the correction inserts arrive; he does not arrange refunds.

script.speaker: W
script.text: Your application mentions coordinating projects overseas. Did that involve managing staff?

Staff development reimbursement — effective January 1
Employees may claim up to $500 per calendar year for approved external courses. Written approval must be obtained before registration. Language courses are eligible only when the employee’s manager confirms a connection to current duties. Travel and meals are excluded.

STAFF TRAVEL POLICY UPDATE

Starting January 1, employees booking rail travel for business trips must use the company travel portal. The portal displays available services and records the fare against the appropriate project. Employees should select a standard-class ticket unless a manager has approved a different class in advance.

A traveler who needs to change a booking should make the change in the portal where possible. If the departure is less than two hours away, the portal may no longer permit changes; in that case, contact the travel desk by telephone. The desk can advise whether the ticket permits a change and whether the rail operator charges a fee.

Receipts for approved additional charges must be uploaded with the expense report. An employee should not purchase a second ticket simply because the first one cannot be changed in the portal. The travel desk will first check whether the original fare can be adjusted or credited.

These instructions apply to rail bookings made after January 1. Tickets purchased before that date remain subject to the conditions shown on the original booking confirmation.

COLLEGE COMMUNITY DAY — VOLUNTEER INFORMATION

The college will hold its annual Community Day on Saturday, May 16, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Local organizations will host demonstrations and information tables in the Student Center. Admission is free, and members of the public do not need to register to visit the tables.

The afternoon shift runs from noon to 4:30 p.m. and includes packing equipment after the event. Volunteers may choose either shift, but they should not sign up for both because the schedules overlap.

A short orientation will be held online on May 12 at 6 p.m. Volunteers who cannot attend should email the Community Office by May 10 to request the recording. The recording covers safety instructions and explains where to collect a name badge on the event day.

CEDAR OFFICE SUPPLIES — SERVICE TERMS
Clients may change the delivery address of an order until noon two business days before dispatch. For orders of at least 80 cartons, delivery is included in the quoted price; smaller orders incur a $45 delivery fee. Orders scheduled for Monday are dispatched on the preceding Friday. A client may request a later dispatch without charge if the request arrives before the address-change deadline.
